ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagrams show a circle centered at O, with A on the circle to the right of O. Segment OA is a radius, and segment AB is drawn tangent to the circle at A, so AB is perpendicular to OA. Point B is above A, segment OB forms angle θ with OA at O, and point C lies on segment OA between O and A. Segment BC is drawn from B to C and is given to bisect angle ABO. Reasoning: Since OA is a radius to the tangent point A, OA ⟂ AB, so triangle AOB is right at A. Also OA = 1 and ∠AOB = θ. In right triangle AOB, OA is adjacent to θ, AB is opposite θ, and OB is the hypotenuse. Thus OB = sec θ and AB = tan θ. Since BC bisects ∠ABO and meets AO at C, the Angle Bisector Theorem gives AC/CO = AB/BO. Therefore AC/CO = tan θ / sec θ = sin θ. Let OC = x. Since OA = 1, AC = 1 - x. Then (1 - x)/x = sin θ. Solving gives 1 - x = x sin θ, so 1 = x(1 + sin θ), and hence x = 1/(1 + sin θ). Therefore OC = 1/(1 + sin θ).

method.method_draft: Set up coordinates and use the distance property of an angle bisector. Place O = (0,0) and A = (1,0), so the tangent at A is the vertical line x = 1. Since ∠AOB = θ, the ray OB has equation y = (tan θ)x and meets x = 1 at B = (1,tan θ). Let C = (x,0), where x = OC. Because C lies on the angle bisector of ∠ABO, its perpendicular distances to the two sides BA and BO are equal. Distance from C to BA, the line x = 1, is 1 - x. Distance from C to BO, the line sin θ·X - cos θ·Y = 0, is x sin θ. Equate: 1 - x = x sin θ, giving x = 1/(1 + sin θ).

claims.source: Therefore AC/CO = tan θ / sec θ = sin θ

claims.claim: Let OC = x.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Let OC = x

claims.claim: AC = 1 - x.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Since OA = 1, AC = 1 - x

claims.claim: (1 - x)/x = sin θ.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Then (1 - x)/x = sin θ

claims.claim: Solving (1 - x)/x = sin θ gives x = 1/(1 + sin θ).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Solving gives 1 - x = x sin θ, so 1 = x(1 + sin θ), and hence x = 1/(1 + sin θ).

claims.claim: OC = 1/(1 + sin θ).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore OC = 1/(1 + sin θ)
